text.p: Pakistan said on Thursday it had suspended 19 ambassadors who had been appointed by the ousted government of prime minister Benazir Bhutto from outside the professional diplomatic service.
The political appointees include the country's ambassadors to the United States, Russia and Britain, France, Germany and Saudi Arabia.
Other envoys affected are those to Bosnia, Brunei, Ghana, Italy, Maldives, the Netherlands, Niger, North Korea, Norway, Switzerland, Tunisia, Uganda and the UNESCO mission in Paris.
A Foreign Ministry spokesman said the caretaker government of Prime Minister Meraj Khalid could still decide to retain any of them if it desired.
He said political ambassadors were appointed with contracts saying they would be deemed to have tendered their resignations when the government that named them was no longer in office.
The caretaker government has already sacked many Bhutto political appointees as well bureaucrats given extensions beyond normal retirement at 60.
